record.oneLiner: A small sauropod sporting a double row of tall neck spines.
record.description: Amargasaurus was a small dicraeosaurid sauropod of Early Cretaceous Argentina, 9–13 m long, known from a nearly complete skeleton. It is unique for two parallel rows of tall spines running down its neck and back — taller than in any other sauropod.

notableFacts.text: Bore two parallel rows of tall neck spines, possibly supporting sails or a horn sheath.
Known from a nearly complete skeleton — rare for a sauropod.
